cover.title: Data export
p3s1i0: This is the screen where you take research data out as files. First choose the type of data you want, then set the scope and options. Types are split into priority 1, 4 types used directly for regulatory submission, and priority 2, 2 supporting types for audit preparation. Export takes time, so it works by submitting a request and receiving a notice when it is complete.
p3.cap.1: Data export hub (SCR-EXP-001) — six type cards and recent history (excluding the left menu)
p3s2i0: “Start export →” — Goes to the scope selection screen for that type 1.2. There is one on each card.
p3s2i1: “View all history →” — Goes to the screen that gathers all past export jobs. Use it to find again a file you have not downloaded.
p3s2i2: The navigation path is Dashboard / Data export.
p3s2i3: Project status banner — Right now it reads “Test data Export … Do not use the output for external submission.” In a project whose operation has ended, it changes to a green “Confirmed data Export”.
p3s2i4: Priority 1 export — “Core clinical data — regulatory submission · source data verification (SDV) · primary data for statistical analysis”.
p3s2i5: Card layout — type name · contents · Start export. Read the description first to see what data is included before you choose (see the table below).
p3s2i6: Priority 2 export — “Supporting and regulatory data — supporting material for regulatory response and audit preparation”.
p3s2i7: Recent export history (up to 5) — Shown from the latest job first. Whether each file has expired is reflected in the download button on its row.
p3s2i8: If you have never exported, this section is empty with the message “No recent export history”.
p3s3.name: Six export types
p3s3r0c2: Entered CRF data, field values and form version information
p3s3r1c2: History of query opened → answered → closed
p3s3r2c2: Subject basic information and status change history
p3s3r3c2: Visit performed · missed · revisit tracking data
p3s3r4c2: Lock · unlock history (two levels: subject · project)
p3s3r5c2: Electronic signature records · 21 CFR Part 11 (cannot be modified or deleted)
p3s4i0: Only data managers and auditors can enter this screen. It does not appear in the left menu for principal investigators · research nurses · monitoring staff · workspace administrators. However, exports remain possible after the project ends, because submission and archive materials still need to be made.
p4.title: Choosing the scope
p4s1i0: Once you choose a type, a screen opens where you decide what to include. You narrow the scope in three ways: Site scope sets the site, presets apply a commonly used combination at once, and in the scope hierarchy tree you check projects, sites and subjects directly. On the right, the period and form filters continue 1.3.
p4.cap.1: Scope selection (SCR-EXP-002), left side — Site scope · presets · scope hierarchy tree (enlarged)
p4s2i0: Site scope — Choose the target site. This selection alone does not narrow the tree below — it is used only to set the target site for a preset.
p4s2i1: Scope presets — Apply a commonly used scope at once. The composition differs by type 2.1 · 2.2.
p4s2i2: Scope hierarchy tree — Check projects, sites and subjects directly. Checking a parent item also selects everything beneath it.
p4s2i3: Scope selection — type name and the contents of that type appear in the title. Check here that you did not enter the wrong type.
p4s2i4: Site scope note — “This selection does not narrow the scope tree below — it is only for setting the target site of the preset (Own Site).”
p4s2i5: Preset note — “Quickly applies commonly used scopes.”
p4s2i6: “Own Site” is shown faded — because the Site scope above is All Sites, no target site has been chosen. Select a site and it becomes active.
p4s2i7: Tree note — “Select by project > site > subject.” Depending on the type, you may select only down to the site level 2.1.
p4s2i8: The number in parentheses next to an item is the number of records under it.
p4s3i0: Choosing a Site scope alone does not narrow the scope. That value only decides which site the “Own Site” preset points to. What is actually exported is what you check in the tree below. If you select only a site and leave the tree empty, nothing will be exported.
p5.title: Filters and estimated size
p5s1i0: On the right is a filter that narrows the tree selection further. The filters differ by type: the period filter is common to all types, and the DataForm filter and Visit filter appear only for types that contain that data. The estimated record count at the bottom of the screen shows the size before you export.
p5.cap.1: Right side of the same screen — period · form · visit filters (enlarged)
p5.cap.2: Bottom of the screen — estimated record count and bottom buttons (full width)
p5s2i0: Period filter — start. If left blank, from the beginning.
p5s2i1: Period filter — end. If left blank, to the end.
p5s2i2: DataForm filter — Exports only specific CRFs. If none is checked, all are included.
p5s2i3: Visit filter — Exports only specific visits. If you select several, data matching any one of them is included.
p5s2i4: Go to export options → — Opens the export options window 3.1.
p5s2i5: The data-existence range is also shown. Dates outside it will return empty results, so look at this range when you choose dates.
p5s2i6: DataForm filter note — “Exports only specific CRFs.”
p5s2i7: Visit filter red warning — “Data not tied to a visit (for example, forms not linked to a visit) is also excluded when you select a visit.”
p5s2i8: Estimated record count — Shows the size before export using three numbers: Subject · records · CRF instances. It is not calculated until you choose a scope.
p5s2i9: Cancel — Discards the scope selection and returns.
p5s3i0: Applying a visit filter also drops data unrelated to visits. The screen itself warns about this in red text. CRFs not tied to a visit can also be dropped while you are trying to receive only specific visits, so for submission exports, leaving the visit filter empty is safer.
p6.title: Query history · Subject
ch2.title: Scope by type
sec2.1.title: Query history · Subject
sec2.2.title: Visit event · Lock · signature
p6s1i0: The scope selection screen looks the same no matter which type you choose. Only the three scope presets and the filter layout on the right change. However, presets that filter by status cannot be clicked right now: the server-side scope contract does not include that condition yet, so pressing them would return the same result as the full scope. To avoid a false sense of security, they are disabled.
p6.cap.1: Query history — OPEN + ANSWERED · CLOSED only (enlarged)
p6s2i0: Presets for Query history — All · OPEN + ANSWERED · CLOSED only. The last two are status-based and currently disabled. To receive only unprocessed queries, select the targets directly in the tree.
p6s2i1: Presets for Subject — All · Own Site · All Terminal subjects. The last one can be used — it selects at once the five subjects that have settled into an ended state (screen failure · early termination · lost to follow-up · death · study ended).
p6s3.name: Presets by type and availability
p6s3r0c1: All · Own Site · All HARD_LOCK subjects
p6s3r2c1: All · Own Site · All Terminal subjects
p6s3r3c1: All · Own Site · scheduled visits only
p6s4i0: Presets that appear faded are not a malfunction. If pressing one gives the same result as the full scope, you would be led to think a filter was applied, so they are disabled on purpose. Hovering the mouse over the button shows the reason. To narrow by that condition, the current method is to select it directly in the scope hierarchy tree.
p7.title: Visit event · Lock · signature
p7s1i0: These are the presets for the priority-2 types and for the visit event. Only the signature history has all three presets active, while the visit event and Lock history have their status-based presets disabled. Even though the types differ, the placement and use of Site scope · scope hierarchy tree · period filter · estimated record count are the same 1.2 · 1.3.
p7.cap.2: Lock history — Subject Lock · Project Lock (enlarged)
p7.cap.3: Signature history — DataInstance signature · DataLock signature (enlarged)
p7s2i0: Visit event — Scheduled visits only is disabled. To receive only scheduled visits, select the visits directly in the Visit filter on the right.
p7s2i1: Lock history — Both Subject Lock and Project Lock are disabled. Because the two levels cannot be separated when you receive them, receive everything, then tell them apart in the file.
p7s2i2: Signature history — DataInstance signature (data signature) and DataLock signature (lock signature) are both available. Use this when you want to receive the signature types separately.
p7s3.name: What changes by type · what stays the same
p7s3i0: What changes — the three scope presets · filter layout on the right · the units you can select in the tree
p7s3i1: The DataForm filter is only in CRF data
p7s3i2: The Visit filter is only in CRF data and Visit event
p7s3i3: For Subject, you select the tree only down to the site level (subject information itself is the export target)
p7s3i4: What stays the same — Site scope · scope hierarchy tree · period filter · estimated record count · bottom buttons
p7s4i0: Lock history cannot be received by level. A request to receive subject locks and project locks separately is not handled by the current presets. Export everything, then tell them apart in the result file. The export itself runs normally.
p8.title: Export option settings
ch3.title: Options and running
sec3.1.title: Export option settings
sec3.2.title: Export in progress
sec3.3.title: Export complete and download
p8s1i0: This window decides how to export after the scope is set. Items are numbered, so you can check them from top to bottom. Defaults alone are enough to export, but for regulatory submission, be sure to check ③ masking and ⑤ archived data inclusion.
p8.cap.1: Export option settings (SCR-EXP-003) — set in number order (enlarged)
p8s2i0: ② File format — Three options: CSV (comma-separated text), Excel (can split into sheets), and ZIP (compresses the results).
p8s2i1: ③ PII masking — Hides values that can identify subjects. Without permission, it is fixed on.
p8s2i2: ④ Unconfirmed data warning — Chooses whether to show a warning or omit the warning when data still being entered is mixed in. Rows are always included either way; only whether a warning is left changes.
p8s2i3: ⑤ Include archived data — Also includes past entries that were kept as archives when the form was significantly revised. For regulatory submission, clear this to receive only the latest version.
p8s2i4: ⑥ Version handling policy — When form versions are mixed, choose between COLUMN_UNION (combine the columns of all versions into one table) and PER_VERSION (a separate file or sheet for each version).
p8s2i5: Run export — Requests the export and moves to the progress screen 3.2.
p8s2i6: ① Export scope — Summarizes the scope set on the previous screen. It cannot be edited here.
p8s2i7: Close — Closes only the option window. The scope selection screen stays as it is.
p8s2i8: Format note — If there are two or more tables, even CSV is automatically bundled into a ZIP for delivery. The request record shows CSV, and you confirm the actual delivery format on the completion screen.
p8s2i9: Masking note — If you do not have permission, it shows “Masking is enforced (cannot be changed)”; if you do, it shows “Can be turned off”. The reason for turning it off is not recorded.
p8s2i10: Archive note — “To receive only the latest version for regulatory submission, clear this.”
p8s2i11: ← Back — Returns to the scope selection screen. The options you set are kept.
p8s3i0: The actual attached files of the CRFs are not included in the ZIP. The table contains only the identifiers of the attachments, so if the original attachments are needed for regulatory submission, collect them through a separate procedure.
p8s3i1: Turning off masking is decided by permission, not by role. Only users with permission to view subject identification information can turn it off, and auditors do not have that permission. Also, the reason for turning it off is not recorded, so when you create a file that contains identifying information, record separately, through your research team's internal procedure, who received it and why.
p9.title: Export in progress
p9s1i0: When you run an export, the screen automatically moves to the job screen. Because the export is processed on the server, it does not finish immediately. This screen refreshes itself every 5 seconds to show progress. Closing the screen does not stop the job — when it completes you receive a notice, and you can find it later in Export history.
p9.cap.1: Downloading the export file (SCR-EXP-006) — right after running, only the progress is shown
p9s2i0: Export in progress — N% and the progress bar.
p9s2i1: The bar shows the progress reported by the server as it is.
p9s2i2: Notice text — “A notice is sent on completion, and this page updates automatically (every 5 seconds).” If automatic updating stops, the text changes to say the job has been interrupted.
p9s2i3: Job number — Starts with ext_. When you contact support, give them this number.
p9s2i4: Running badge — changes to Completed when done 3.3.
p9s2i5: Summary of export type and scope — “1 Site (020A) · CSV”.
p9s2i6: Performer · run time · record count · format. The record count shows — until the export finishes.
p9s3i0: Closing the screen does not cancel the export. You can do other work without waiting, and you will receive a notice when it completes. If you miss the notice, find the same job number in the recent export history on the Data export screen or in View all history, and download it.
p10.title: Export complete and download
p10s1i0: When the export finishes, the same screen changes to the completed state. The file is not stored permanently on the server and has an expiration date — after it expires, you need to export again. The completion screen also shows warnings from the export process and an integrity verification value that lets you check that the file has not been damaged.
p10.cap.1: Export complete — download · expiration · export warnings · integrity check
p10s2i1: Re-run with same options — Exports again with the same scope and options. Use it after the expiration date has passed.
p10s2i2: Completed badge — While in progress it was Running.
p10s2i3: File name — Includes the job number, so you can match it against the history.
p10s2i4: Size · record count · format. The format shows CSV → ZIP because the file was packed automatically, as there are two or more tables 3.1.
p10s2i5: Expiration — The download link expires after this time.
p10s2i6: N export warnings — The export succeeded, but there is something you should know. Examples are: there was no masking target · data that was not yet finished was included · the file was compressed because there are several tables. The server's own sentences are shown as they are.
p10s2i7: Integrity check (SHA-256) — Expands to show the file's fingerprint value. Use it to check that the downloaded file was not damaged in transit.
p10s2i8: Summary of export type and scope — the same place as on the in-progress screen.
p10s3i0: Do not submit without reading the export warnings. A warning is not a failure, but it can tell you that data still being entered was mixed in, or that masking was not actually applied. If the export is for regulatory submission, check every warning, and if needed fix the cause and export again.
p11.title: The downloaded file
ch4.title: Output files
sec4.1.title: The downloaded file
p11s1i0: This shows the file as it looks after you open the download. This is not a system screen but the result file after you download it. If there are several tables, they are packed into one ZIP with one CSV per table, and the file name includes the job number, so you can tell which export it came from.
p11.cap.1: The downloaded ZIP and the CSV inside it, opened (not a SMART-EDC screen)
p11s2i0: The ZIP file name includes the job number — the same as the number on the completion screen 3.3.
p11s2i1: The archive contains one CSV per table. Apart from the main table, subtables are separated out. It contains only tables; the CRF attachment files themselves are not included (see Precautions in 3.1).
p11s2i2: Opening it in Excel shows a “Data may be lost” notice — this is a property of CSV, and the original file is unchanged. Take care only when you edit and save.
p11s2i3: The first row contains the column names — it starts with instance, subject, form code, form version and occurrence number, followed by the entered value columns.
p11s2i4: Starting from the second row is the actual data. Each row is one record.
p11s3i0: Do not save the CSV as is in Excel. Excel can change values when saving, for example by converting long numbers to scientific notation or deleting leading zeros. Only check the contents and close, or if you need to process it, keep the original separately and work on a copy. For regulatory submission, use the downloaded original.
